◘ 14 May: the National Day of Remembrance of the martyrs of the communist prisons
◘ The icon “The Mother of God with the Saints of the Prisons”, in the ossuary of the “Exaltation of the Holy Cross” Hermitage in Aiud, inspired the icon painted on glass that I am showing you today
◘ A few words about two of the places where Romanian martyrs were tortured by the communist secret police:
 • Râpa Robilor (the Slaves' Ravine) is the place where, with no graves and no crosses, the tortured bodies of the confessors of Aiud prison were thrown by the communist torturers, so that they could never be identified.
On this ground, sanctified by the blood of Romanian martyrs, stands the monument “The Calvary of Aiud” (a temple of suffering and pain), raised in memory of the political prisoners of the communist persecution of 1947–1964
 • The former prison in Pitești, known as “the Pitești Experiment”, is the place where, through beatings, humiliation and brutal torture inflicted daily in order to “totally re-educate” the political prisoners (mostly students, intellectuals and members of political parties), the prisoners in fact broke down mentally or died. The essence of the method used at Pitești was to turn victims into executioners, torture being regarded as a mere means, not an end. Everything that happened at Pitești was so horrifying that it goes beyond the limits of imagination... A survivor of “the Pitești experiment” told me about it (everything that happened there, and in other prisons where he was interrogated and tortured); despite the terrifying torture he endured, he managed to remain dignified, whole and upright
 • Other places where Romanians were tortured were marked by the use of torture to convert them to communist ideology. These were at Suceava, Pitești, Gherla, Târgu Ocna, Târgșor, Brașov and Ocnele Mari. The prisons for exterminating the political and intellectual elite: Sighet, Râmnicu Sărat, Galați, Aiud, Craiova, Brașov, Oradea, Pitești. Labour camps: the Danube–Black Sea Canal (Peninsula, Poarta Albă, Salcia, Periprava, Constanța, Midia, Capul Midia, Cernavodă, etc.). Interrogation prisons: Rahova, Malmaison, Uranus

a72795792642:
• «Saint George the Great Martyr» in an icon painted on glass in our workshop (model: Țara Oltului, first half of the 19th century → a charming depiction, like a fairy tale “told” in colours painted on glass ❤)

• Γεώργιος, Ágios Geórgios, or George – versions: Georgiu, Georz, Giurgiu, Iorgu, from the Greek Georgios – was a Roman general of Greek origin and an officer in the Guard of the Roman emperor Diocletian, who was sentenced to death for refusing to renounce the Christian faith. As a Christian martyr he later became one of the most venerated saints of Christianity, and was especially venerated by the crusaders. Saint George is remembered by almost all the traditional Churches, usually on 23 April. He is considered the patron of many countries, regions and cities. (Wikipedia)

✧ 2024, the Year of Avram Iancu: Avram Iancu, celebrated 200 years after his birth and 152 years after his death.

• Avram Iancu, the future national hero, was born in 1824. The exact date of his birth was not recorded, but according to the hero himself he was born "in cherry time". Since cherries ripen later in the mountains because of the harsher climate, he may have been born in July or August.

• The work I am showing you today depicts Avram Iancu – “the Little Prince of the Mountains” – with Crișan, Cloșca and Horea beside Horea's Oak.
This painting on glass is inspired by a mural in the Orthodox church of “the Dormition of the Mother of God” at the Țebea Memorial Complex

•The Testament of Avram Iancu
“My last will!
The only longing of my life is to see my Nation happy, for which I have worked as far as I could until now, sadly without much success; indeed, just now I see with sorrow that my hopes and the sacrifice I made are turning to nothing.
I do not know how many days I may have left; a kind of foreboding seems to tell me that the future is uncertain. I therefore wish and firmly decree that after my death all my property, movable and immovable, shall pass to the benefit of the Nation, to help found an academy of law, for I firmly believe that those who fight with the weapon of the law will be able to win the rights of my Nation. "

~ The Nativity of the Mother of God ~ Icon on glass (model: Nicula, early 19th century)🌸
 About the icon:
" Lying on a bed above which hangs a rich curtain, Saint Anne has the baby girl at her feet. Joachim urges her to eat from the dishes he brings. A border with the rope motif surrounds the composition. The novelty of the image lies in the way the floor is drawn, like a roof of curved tiles, which focuses all attention on Joachim's gesture." (Source of the description: National Institute of Heritage)

° The icon is not available; it was painted for a holy and beautiful Orthodox Church in Romania
